before: Prerequisite: required fields and connected help. pattern constrains the entire nonempty value of a supported text input. Here [A-Z] means one uppercase ASCII letter, [0-9] one digit, and {2} repeats the preceding set twice. required separately rejects blank input.

aria-invalid="true" communicates a known error; it does not create or clear native validity. aria-describedby lists IDs of help/error text. This is a static invalid-state snapshot, not an automatic error updater. A real form must update the message and state after correction and revalidate on the server.

```html

Use two uppercase letters followed by two digits, such as AB12.

The entered code has lowercase letters. Change them to uppercase.

```

```html

Use two uppercase letters followed by two digits, such as AB12.

The code format is now valid.

``` ARIA communicates an error state; the pattern still examines the actual value. Change both the value and the feedback when correction succeeds.
Optional: change one relevant value, predict the effect, and compare the parsed attributes. Structural checks do not prove browser presentation or accessibility.
after: `pattern` sets a text rule for an input. Here, `[A-Z]{2}[0-9]{2}` means two uppercase English letters followed by two digits. The whole nonempty entry must match. `required` separately stops the field being left blank.

`aria-invalid="true"` tells assistive tools that the field has an error. It does not check the value itself. `aria-describedby` connects the field to text that explains the rule and how to fix the mistake.

This example shows a field with a known mistake. ```html

Use two uppercase letters followed by two digits, such as AB12.

The entered code has lowercase letters. Change them to uppercase.

``` `ab12` has lowercase letters, so it does not match the pattern. `code-help` explains the rule. `code-error` tells the person to change the letters to uppercase. The field points to both messages.

When the person corrects the value to `AB12`, the feedback should change too. Set `aria-invalid` to false or remove it, and remove or update the old error message. HTML alone does not keep that message up to date; a later JavaScript lesson can add that behavior.

Build the shown error example. Keep the starting value `ab12`, the exact pattern, and `required`. Add the label, help and error paragraphs. Connect both paragraph ids with `aria-describedby="code-help code-error"`. Run the checks. This task deliberately starts with an incorrect entry so you can practise helpful feedback.
